answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The glacier multiplier is published, charged in nebula, and ferrous lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 996 identities would post 2803 proofs and burn roughly 59 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
